name: Tricep Pushdown
description: The tricep pushdown is a cable isolation exercise for the triceps performed by pushing a rope or bar attachment downward from a high pulley. It trains all three heads of the triceps with the rope variation providing additional wrist pronation at the bottom that may improve medial and lateral head activation.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a high cable pulley holding a rope or bar attachment at chest height. Elbows tucked at the sides, upper arms stationary.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the pulley to the highest position. Use a rope for greater range of motion and contraction, or a straight bar for heavier loading.
steps: Push the attachment downward by extending the elbows fully.
With a rope: rotate hands outward at the bottom for maximum tricep contraction.
Return under control to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on extension, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Allowing the elbows to drift forward and away from the sides
Leaning forward excessively — maintain an upright torso
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full elbow extension at the bottom. Return to 90-degree elbow angle or slightly more at the top.
coaching_cues: Keep your elbows glued to your sides — only your forearms move
Spread the rope at the bottom for a full tricep squeeze
